craft_claim: The inspirational voice raises perceived self-efficacy mainly through vicarious models and specific verbal persuasion about capability, since enactive mastery cannot be supplied by text.

supporting_evidence.note: Bandura derives efficacy expectations from four sources: performance accomplishments, vicarious experience, verbal persuasion, and physiological states; enactive mastery is most dependable, vicarious/modelled experience next.

supporting_evidence.location: Opening address, World's Parliament of Religions, 11 September 1893
supporting_evidence.note: Vivekananda's direct address converts a stranger-audience into kin and frames a shared forward project, functioning as verbal persuasion of collective capability.

counterevidence.note: Verbal persuasion in the form of repeated positive self-statements backfired for low-self-esteem participants, so persuasion is not uniformly beneficial.

scope: Instructional, aspirational, and copy prose; strongest when a concrete model is available.
exceptions: Audiences with low domain self-esteem may resist vicarious comparison; compressing the model's distance or changing to compassionate register is required.
